subject: Delta 001 to brief MSD-001: Ziggy's three answers (the man on the dune gets the tone; baritone; voices permitted in an invented tongue, prepared as two variants, not yet placed)
body:
Ziggy answered the three open questions of the brief's section 6 within the hour (his words in the source line). Read the attached delta with the brief; where they differ, the delta rules; the brief's file is unchanged, so its hash in 46ebf08b stays true. The direction sheet and the cue map changed (dated lines with his answers); their new hashes are in the delta's section 4 and supersede the brief's section 8 for those two files.

In short: (1) the man on the dune gets the one sustained low tone, the default; drop the silence-only variant. (2) The register is baritone; write baritone saxophone; drop the tenor and alto swaps; the tower's variants line reads none. (3) Voices are permitted, but only in an invented tongue no one on screen speaks and no listener understands: no real language's words, no translatable lyric, no written syllables, the instruments still the piece, off-screen by construction and placed only where no mouth is on screen. The name he used to point at that idea is a franchise name and enters no prompt or return; his link is not a source; the delta gives the idea in plain words. He has not said which cue carries the voice, so the three final prompts stay instrumental and you add one voice sentence each for the sandworm (under the tracks, before the haze lifts) and the vault (a whisper above the drones from the ladder to the door), each with the one do-not line that replaces "no vocals" when swapped in, under variants, not merged, at the places and loudness the delta gives; default wording "a woman's low voice"; the tower gets none. The delta lists which brief lines it rereads, including the completion check and the generation note's by-ear check.

Nothing else changes: same return path, same conversation, reply to 46ebf08b with path, sha256 and bytes; one receipt covering both messages is fine. Still open for Ziggy, not for you: which cue carries the voice, and whose voice it is.

attachments.description: Delta 001 to brief MSD-001: the three answers verbatim; what changes for the drafter; the voice as an invented tongue with the franchise name kept out; two voice variants proposed and not merged, each with its do-not line; the brief lines reread; what stays open for Ziggy.

source: Ziggy, typed in Claude's session on 2026-10-28 at about 06:05 UTC, verbatim: "The man on the dune: one sustained low tone after the burst" / "The saxophone's register: baritone" / "voices can be heard, but it would be in the tongue of the Bene Gesserit https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bene_Gesserit"
